title: AEO Trade Facilitation and International Cooperation
summary: The scope of AEO benefits expanded to include advanced trade facilitation measures like comprehensive guarantees and electronic green channel access. Additionally, the framework now explicitly provides for Mutual Recognition Agreements (MRAs) to facilitate international trade.

evolution.Benefits: Expanded from basic physical examination waivers to advanced financial and electronic facilitation.
evolution.International Scope: Added formal legal basis for international reciprocity via MRAs.

timeline.change: Introduction of comprehensive guarantees and self-assessment for green channel AEOs.

Customs Act 1969: Section 43 of this Act provides the legal basis for the acceptance of comprehensive guarantees for customs purposes.
Comprehensive Guarantee: This mechanism allows for the consolidated coverage of customs duties and charges, provided that the total value of the guarantee is not less than the cumulative duties and taxes payable on the goods.
It is applicable to Authorized Economic Operators, government entities, and organizations specified by the National Board of Revenue, as well as for transit and transshipment operations.
The instrument must be in the form of a bank guarantee when such a guarantee is otherwise required for the clearance of goods.
It is prohibited to use a comprehensive guarantee for operations, declarations, or customs procedures that involve two or more different types of guarantee requirements.
Authorized Economic Operator: These entities are explicitly eligible to utilize the comprehensive guarantee facility for their customs operations.
National Board of Revenue: The Board has the authority to specify which institutions, in addition to Authorized Economic Operators and government bodies, are permitted to provide comprehensive guarantees.
Transit and Transshipment: These operations are explicitly eligible for coverage under the comprehensive guarantee regime.

Customs Act 1969: Section 90(3) of the Act serves as the legal foundation for implementing self-assessment procedures for specific categories of goods declarations.
Customs Assessment: Self-assessment is applicable for goods declarations filed by Authorized Economic Operators, low-risk goods identified through automated risk management, or specific entities authorized by the National Board of Revenue.
When performing self-assessment, required documentation must be submitted to the appropriate officer either directly or via the customs computerized system prior to final assessment.

If credible intelligence or complaints exist regarding a self-assessed declaration, or upon a voluntary request by the importer, exporter, or their agent, the appropriate officer must conduct the assessment process according to prescribed rules.
Authorized Economic Operator: Authorized Economic Operators utilizing the electronic green channel are eligible to utilize self-assessment procedures for their goods declarations.
National Board of Revenue: The Board holds the authority to designate specific persons or entities eligible for self-assessment through the issuance of official orders or notifications.
Customs Computerised Entry Processing Sy: The customs computerized system serves as the primary electronic platform for submitting goods declarations and required documentation for the purpose of self-assessment.

১৫। অন্য দেশের সহিত চুক্তি।—(১)  বোর্ড অথরাইজড ইকোনমিক অপারেটর প্রোগ্রাম এর আওতায় পারস্পরিক ভিত্তিতে বাংলাদেশে স্বীকৃতিপ্রাপ্ত caravan এর অপর দেশে একই ধরনের সুবিধা প্রাপ্তির শর্তে অন্য কোনো দেশের caravan কে বাংলাদেশে অনুরূপ সুবিধা প্রদানের লক্ষ্যে উক্ত দেশের সহিত পারস্পরিক স্বীকৃতি চুক্তি [Mutual Recognition Agreement (MRA)] স্বাক্ষর করিতে পারিবে।
(২) বিধি (১) অনুসারে উক্ত স্বীকৃতি চুক্তির আওতায় অন্য দেশের স্বীকৃতিপ্রাপ্ত caravan এর জন্য চুক্তির শর্ত মোতাবেক পারস্পরিক ভিত্তিতে অথরাইজড ইকোনমিক অপারেটর সুবিধা প্রদান ও শর্তাবলি নির্ধারণের জন্য বোর্ড আদেশ জারি করিতে পারিবে।

National Board of Revenue: The National Board of Revenue is authorized to enter into mutual recognition agreements with other countries to ensure reciprocal benefits for authorized economic operators.
The board is empowered to issue orders to grant authorized economic operator benefits and define terms and conditions for entities recognized by foreign countries under these reciprocal agreements.
Authorized Economic Operator: Authorized economic operators are subject to mutual recognition agreements that allow them to receive corresponding benefits in other countries based on reciprocal arrangements.

Benefits and operational conditions for foreign-recognized authorized economic operators are determined by the National Board of Revenue through formal orders following the signing of mutual recognition agreements.
Mutual Recognition Agreement: A mutual recognition agreement is a formal treaty between the government and a foreign country designed to grant reciprocal trade facilitation benefits to authorized economic operators.
These agreements serve as the legal framework under which the National Board of Revenue can extend specific operational advantages to foreign entities recognized under the program.

member_objects.resolved_text: ১. বোর্ড বিধিমালার বিধি ১৫(১) অনুসারে অথরাইজড ইকোনমিক অপারেটর প্রোগ্রাম এর আওতায় অন্য দেশের সাথে পারস্পরিক স্বীকৃতি চুক্তি [Mutual Recognition Agreement (MRA)] স্বাক্ষর করতে পারবে এবং চুক্তির বাস্তবায়নের জন্য আদেশ জারি করতে পারবে।

National Board of Revenue: In accordance with the relevant rules, the Board is authorized to sign mutual recognition agreements with other countries under the Authorized Economic Operator programme and issue directives to implement such agreements.
Mutual Recognition Agreement: The Board is empowered to enter into mutual recognition agreements with foreign customs administrations to support the objectives of the Authorized Economic Operator programme.
Authorized Economic Operator: The Authorized Economic Operator programme serves as the framework under which the Board can establish mutual recognition agreements with international counterparts.
